title: Rafi and the Long Boat
blurb: Five children, one river race and a boat that leaks. Can Rafi's team stop arguing in time?

chapters.title: The Challenge
chapters.text:
Every year in September, the river village of Muara Teduh held a boat race. The older boys and girls usually won, and everybody expected it again. This year, though, the headman made a surprising announcement. "Children from eight to ten may enter a team of five," he said. "You must build your own boat."

Rafi's heart jumped. He had always dreamed of racing. He quickly gathered his friends: Tiara, who was clever with numbers, strong Anto, tiny but brave Wulan, and Dodi, who could not stop telling jokes.

"We have three weeks," said Rafi. "Let us show everybody what we can do."

chapters.title: Building the Boat
chapters.text:
The children began on Monday after school. Tiara measured the river and drew a plan on a piece of cardboard. "A long, narrow boat moves faster than a wide one," she explained. "Water has less to push against."

Anto's uncle gave them old planks of wood. Wulan, who was the smallest, crawled into tight corners to hammer in the nails. Dodi sang silly songs to keep everyone happy.

After ten days, the boat was finished. It was a little crooked, but it was long and bright blue. On the side, Rafi painted its name in white letters: The Swift Fish.

"She is beautiful," Wulan whispered.

chapters.title: A Hole in the Plan
chapters.text:
On Saturday, the children carried The Swift Fish down to the river for a test. The water was smooth and green. They climbed in, grabbed their paddles and pushed away from the bank.

For a minute, everything was perfect. Then Dodi looked down. "Er, why are my socks wet?" he asked.

Water was bubbling up through a gap between two planks. Within seconds, it reached their ankles. "Paddle to the bank!" shouted Rafi. The boat sank in the shallow water with a soft glug.

The five children stood in the river, soaked and silent. Even Dodi had no joke. The race was only ten days away.

chapters.title: Too Many Plans
chapters.text:
That evening, the children met in Rafi's yard. Nobody knew how to fix the leak.

"We should paint the gaps with thick glue," said Anto. "We should start again with new wood," said Tiara. "We should find some tar," said Rafi. Everyone talked at the same time, and their voices grew louder and louder.

"You never listen to me!" Tiara shouted. "You always think your idea is best!"

"That is not true!" said Rafi, and his face turned red.

Wulan covered her ears. Dodi sat quietly in a corner. Soon Tiara and Rafi walked home without saying goodbye. The team had fallen apart.

chapters.title: The Race
chapters.text:
The next morning, Rafi could not sleep. He knew that he had not listened to Tiara. He walked to her house and said, "I am sorry. Please tell me your idea."

Tiara smiled. "I am sorry too. We can do all our ideas. We will use the glue and the tar for the gaps, and we will not need new wood."

All week, the five friends worked together. They used glue, then tar, and Wulan tested every plank. On race day, The Swift Fish stayed dry.

The big teams paddled fast, but the children kept a steady rhythm: one, two, one, two. They came second, only a boat's length behind the winners. "Second place!" cried Dodi. "Who needs a joke? That was already funny!" Everybody laughed.
